answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public, slashable bond before it can vote or claim rewards. Repeated identities then do not create free influence: each one ties up more capital, and provable double-voting or fabricated attestations burn the bond. The garden of agents may welcome a comet of new entrants, but a prism of independent reviewers should verify misconduct before slashing, so honest newcomers are not punished merely for being numerous.
